2026年4月10日更新。 这是一款非常非常好的游戏。我没想到的是，都过去那么久了，制作组竟然还持续保持更新。跟市面上很多卖完游戏，几个月后就消失、不再更新的团队，完全不同！ 我现在有一点需要制作组知道，不知道能否被看到： 铸誓会的火焰圣女，其注能专长是：她获得1层注能时，其他所有队伍成员也获得1层注能。 我试了很多次，这次注能专长是无效的。她获得注能后，什么事情也没发生，只是显示她获得注能了。 我让其他单位不注能，只有她注能的前提下，我发现了其他单位全都没有因此获得注能层数，也没有激活对应的注能能力。 请修复这个BUG。 ------------------------------ 最新： 1.那个科技，名字好像叫“冲击碎片”。在敌人失衡状态下，添加额外失衡会导致敌人获得相当于额外失衡的0.5倍的破裂。这类破裂从未出现过，我试过好多次了。 2.科技“涌血娃娃”，破裂伤害会产生“溅射”伤害，无论是敌人进入失衡状态的那一刻，还是敌人在失衡状态被添加破裂，这个“溅射”伤害从未出现过。 3.电起源的传统重炮手，当前回合留存牌会获得爆炸弹药。那么为何自动攻击的“溅射”伤害，只有基础攻击力的一半。我提升的临时攻击力都不计入的。那这个溅射伤害就只有固定“2点”伤害，有和没有，几乎都一样。而且这个溅射伤害还不能暴击，即使敌人失衡了，露出弱点了，溅射伤害也没有暴击。这是否是BUG？要知道注能起源的重炮手，溅射伤害是把临时攻击力也计入的。 请把这些BUG修改掉，否则很影响体验。 ------------ 我已经玩了Beta版本大几十个小时了。游戏即将出品的那几天一直都蹲着数日子。 买来后，玩了1小时，我退款了，我觉得和Beta版本差别不大，而我已经有些腻味了。 后来想了想，毕竟玩了快100小时了，还不付钱，这样也不好。就花了100元买下。 今天又玩了玩，发现改变还是挺多的，这100块钱算是买到惊喜了。 ------------ 目前就用电的起源是足够好的，我已经通关难度5了。 但是第一个用注能的起源，不够好。 为什么电好？ 1.电可以存电量，不像红石每一轮必须用完。 2.电可以很容易做到刷费用刷抽卡，红石给费给卡的牌少并且性价比不高 3.电可以存卡，下回合的存卡是必然的，轻易做到联动和combo。红石的换卡是不确定的。 4.电即使存很多了，卡够用了，也有可以一口气用光的X费卡，非常灵活 总而言之，电起源，可以做场、可以进行资源的管理和循环，可以一回合不断刷费用和刷卡。个别2张卡联动就能打出非常惊人的效果，比如 回响+X费用的电束，直接上百点伤害。比如 科技重复引擎+升级后的锁定光束，直接1张卡用0费的方式反复打3次，每次11点血。 而注能起源，各兵种各打各的，不仅无法资源管理，单张卡的力度都很弱。电起源的灯塔每轮给护罩，注能的灯塔就摆设不会动的，2费的6护盾+1轮自动攻击，简直是犯罪啊。注能派系的灯塔牌基本上都是污染卡池的垃圾，只有注能卡勉强用用。 还请提高一些注能派，否则高难度基本就是活受罪。
话说那些必须要神恩的卡能不能再设置个没有神恩时的效果，要不然和伤口似的都不敢多拿

大量的随机攻击使得防御卡牌的价值大幅下降 羸弱的神器效果，过低的回合费用，有限的过牌能力，稀有的删牌服务，导致combo艰难，你只能倾向于一直拿强单卡 实际上是想打“中评”的但是没有这种选项，以肉鸽游戏来说它有一种“魂游”的倾向，比起让你玩得爽它更想要难到你 保护灯塔的设计也很失败，玩到现在几乎没有因为灯被打空了输的全是前面的角色死完了 局外成长基本=没有 灯塔牌相对于它的费用获取难度来说，效果不够强，升级机会更是重量级，点名圣光屏障，升级前基本等于污染卡池的卡，除非他带一个指向性嘲讽效果不然就是纯垃圾卡 一般战斗你舍不得用灯塔牌，导致很多时候抽到就是手牌-1 总结：肉鸽来说很失败，肉鸽游戏应该是越了解游戏、周目数越高难度越低的，但这款显然不是 6/10 肉鸽类型游戏的起始分数应该是7

半成品，我开了加1能量和多抽一张牌的模式打深度2都打得想死。我玩红钩的黑暗地牢1+2都没觉得有什么问题，它看脸但是它连招没问题啊。你这个灯卡纯纯废物卡，没有神恩的情况下简直就是乐色，多周目的小兵都没什么成长的，反而抽这么多小队出来，多人出战就是污染卡池，一套连招根本就没什么机会搞出来，看了其他人的评论拿个领航员单刷真的强，因为他单刷抽都是自己的卡。 这个卡升级你自己算过吗？一轮按十个回合算，了不起升级两三张还不能指定升级哪个角色的。打怪也是随机打，非要上一个锁定，而且没有位移牌遇到那种一下搞你几十点血的你半点都动不了。你只能追求迅速的解决敌人，以至于防御牌和笑话一样。策划你自己玩过吗？你真的深度5自己通关过吗？高难度还回血就一点点，我觉得要不然那个医疗点你撤了吧，商店里面给多搞点低价绷带算了。

感觉太简单了

虽然只开放了两个体系，但组合很丰富。每个兵种的牌库和专长、以及影响全队的科技(遗物)等，决策点很多。高难度下SL量可想而知的大。相应的，对SL的次数进行了软限制这点也很不错，避免了过于钻牛角尖把大量时间耗费在SL上。我个人很喜欢这点。 同一个兵种，在不同体系中并不是简单的换皮，而是配合体系做了一套新卡组。队伍成型的途径比较多样，这一块真挺不错的。 缺点是信息的透明度很低，而且都能通过SL简单的规避。很多人也说这个城市卡的部分很糟糕，初见根本不知道什么效果。我当然可以先点进去看一眼再SL，那为什么不直接告诉我呢。点进商店发现钱不够，退出来什么都不做，人物卡就消耗掉了。或者道具卡虽然不消耗但只能等下个回合再用了，诸如此类的设计我都很讨厌。
比怪物火车好玩

finish all level in about 2 hour, then what to do next? just trying new unit and ascension (in a level you've already completed). if you're looking for lots of unique level run, this game not for you. be prepared to read overwhelming amount of keyword/stat/buff/debuff/whateverelse, you'll likely will read more than playing in your first couple of run.

除了美术以外一无是处………… 能把游戏性，上瘾性，游玩乐趣上全不点，全点在美术上也是太让人费解…… 两个小时下来没有感觉到一丝一毫的正面反馈， 纯属在摸索各种机制各种系统， 主城建设，剧情，兵种，战棋，每一个都做得不行，平均线以下， 还能玩什么。。 哪怕是你做不出来好玩法，你不会做卡牌， 你往强化剧情的方面，弄配音，做世界观也好啊。。 比如你搞末世，绝望，孤城，人类最后希望什么的， 但你氛围压根一点没有啊…… 明黄色主色调，配乐也好，各方面细节也罢，全都是礼拜天在公园享受晨光的观感， 真的吗？你末世，整一个教堂配色？明艳，黄白，暖色调，就打一个舒心？ 这直接让人想起以前碰过的 Gremlins Inc，这个色调就是符合那类文艺复兴，或是维多利亚时期，节奏缓慢， 比如一个绅士，淑女在阳伞下喝下午茶 ——但你把这个色调放在末世，地下，人类灭亡前夕…… 把多数暖色调，换成钢铁，深蓝，蓝灰色，黑铁那些的色调， 整个氛围都才能摆脱掉欢乐卡牌的氛围，不然真的一点点绝望感没有。。 哪怕是克苏鲁系的，暗黑地牢都可以学一下啊？ 至少把地下黑暗的氛围做出来啊？ 甚至一样是突发奇想搞3D的，最近玩的污痕圣杯（Tainted Grail: Conquest） 那边的确把3D做的很一般，大地图和模式有问题， 但氛围到了，配音也不错，增色本身就不错的剧情，游戏可玩性也可以，就真的不会太差， 几个不差，有出彩的部分，组合起来就可以玩几十个小时了。 甚至于抛开一部分蒸汽朋克，不管正不正统， 整那种 “大即美” 疯狂的工业氛围，去参照魔幻苏联题材，魔幻二战的风格， 套进异世界也好些啊。。 而不是凭空创造一个平平无奇的美术体系…… 真的是哪怕做的不错了，不符合末世绝望，求生，那就完全不合适，甚至投入那么多直接血本无归了， 而且你们做的城镇建设，就只是个NPC对话模拟器，没有一丝种田， 战斗，也平平无奇的淡如白水， 没剧情， 除了复杂的体系机制啥也没有。。 你这定价，成本全在制作3D和美术上吧？ 这不是骗没玩过肉鸽萌新的钱吗？ 更别提还有那么多 “评测”，好评率高的不符合现实。。 玩过真的好肉鸽的人看来，真的难以下咽， 更别提我最近才入雪居之地，大鱼大肉之后跟我讲君子之交淡如水？ 甚至连刚好一起买的 Deathless Tales of Old Rus，它玩法勉强，但美术和氛围也吊打了你们……至少不会不值那个价，至少能玩多少小时，总体体验还过得去。

这是一个中差评，14个小时，已经打到下行7了。 作为一款肉鸽卡牌游戏，100多块的定价我觉得绝大多数都出在了美术上。 作为抢先体验的版本，其内容过少，没有固定的删牌手段和选择角色牌的手段，导致build太难成型。 在高难度下的运营，导致我的盟友牌不得不每用一次，就SL一次。 尤其是，当我精打细算下，多余的盟友牌居然没有地点用，太搞笑了。 战斗难度和战斗惩罚已经很高了，就没有必要在资源下抠抠索索的吧？ 然后就是商店，购买专长还要我盟友属性解锁？本来资源就少赚钱就难。 抽卡随机，删卡随机，专长随机，发育随机，为什么商店种类也搞随机？ 总之玩到哪里都不爽，制作者为什么要想方设法就让我们玩家不爽呢？ Ps:全程都是强弩手在输出。
重复且机械，目前内容确实不够 玩过一把不会想再开的肉鸽卡牌 注能机制设计的太狗屎了，能量点是稀缺资源，注能卡牌却给得很多，每场战斗都在卡手 而且每种注能卡设计得，区分度真挺小吧
还不错 但是单位和卡牌有点少

Sorry, but lowering the price in early access is a ♥♥♥♥ you move to all early buyers. They handed out one free copy of the game to the inventory of all early buyers as a "Thank you"? Stop. This shouldn't be labeled as a "Thank you". It should be labeled as a "Sorry". While As We Descend is a good game (for early access), this move clearly shows what's most important for these devs: Money. They set the price WAY too high in the beginning. People told them, and they did not give a ♥♥♥♥ for over three months. Just because not enough people bought it, they have now lowered the price in the hope of getting more money. I'm pretty sure this won't help much. They're either gonna abandon the game or push it out of early access half assed, mark my words. Don't give them any money right now. They just showed how they treat the community. I'd rather have a refund than a second copy of this game.
一直以来玩起来都是比较痛苦的，资源少，队员灯火共用卡池，怪物力度强， 也一直在纠结到底给什么评价 更新后游戏性增加不少，特别是灯火卡牌替换机制让游戏体验上了一个台阶 做游戏，就是要每一次更新都更在玩家的爽点上，大家是来玩游戏的，不是来受苦的

这游戏给我一种感觉，折磨。道具和灯火卡互相卡，灯火卡和神恩资源互相卡，一堆神恩卡跟粘液一样沾手上，我都把卡组拉得每个角色3张卡了也转不动卡组。角色卡互相卡。非推荐少上角色，啥毛病呢，我拿了角色就是为了看他卡面是吧，资源猛猛卡，养个大哥这个吃力，怪的技能一个赛一个猛，全体12的aoe，我怎么防，你这个资源卡的程度，我拿得到aoe群盾卡吗。打完12一看下个难度，疲劳就得病，我养大哥就把把治疲劳，就非得嚯嚯我那几十的金币是吧神经病，不养大哥你教教我怎么打。打完12难度就不想再重新开一把了，感觉自己给自己坐牢。我也不知道你非得卡你那个资源显得那么有深度干啥，把把感觉自己就是残疾人。网上最近一个视频攻略还是半个月前的，人都麻了。反正有新意，但是折磨，入坑建议自己找找视频，三思
商店一直不补充资源。感觉好鸡肋。还有灯火为什么是固定8张卡位不能删？强行稀释key牌上手率？
还可以挺好玩 但是不知道为什么一个单机卡牌游戏这么防着玩家 作为一个轻度玩家随便玩玩想用修改器修改一下数据 修改一下存档爽完耽误厂商赚钱了吗？对数据层层加密层层校验显得很小气

I don't recommend this game for reasons I'll get into later, but I originally bought the game because it has: - A distinct and beautiful art style - A fantastic UI - Excellent creatures - An enticing world - Card-based gameplay Why I can't recommend this game is because I simply don't know where I am, or why things are the way they are, or even why I should care about the things I do in the game. I don't know if I'm in the past or the future. I have no idea about anything, and therefore I don't care about anything. Why are lanterns important? Who am i? Who is the tall spirit lady in the centre of the city? For a game that has extremely capable artists at the helm, there seems to be no effort made to tell the story of such a seemingly rich and interesting world. Context for any of what's happening seems to be completely missing, and if I was supposed to read the answers to all the above questions in some bit of text at the start, then I must have missed it. With artists of this calibre, you shouldn't be telling a story of the world and its characters through text. Just sayin'. I would want to see a storyboarded sequence at the very least, and not just at the start but all the way through it. I want to trust characters who then turn on me depending on what choices I make through the game. I want this to impact on the gameplay. I want to be challenged by the very forces I've sworn to protect, and question the nature of the world itself. Get philosophical with it. Go crazy. But the fact that there isn't even any kind of evolution to the story beyond what may or may not have been explained at the start means that essentially there is no story, so there's no point to any of the beautiful things we're seeing through the game. There seems to be factions in the city, and a tension between the upper class/clergy and the workers. Does that impact on anything in the game to any substantive degree? Is the lady at the centre of the city an entity with free will, or some psychic manifestation made to protect the city? Does the lady have any relationship to the lanterns that we collect? Do we ever see the lanterns engaged or fulfil their purpose? Why is the city built on a huge well? How are the people in the city not completely traumatized by the absurd situation they're in, and just go around acting as if everything is normal? What is beyond the city and the well? Why is the world outside so corrupted? Where does the spirit lady come from? And how far down does the well go? Like, none of this is expanded upon. Combat is this: Pick the best cards we're dealt with and wait (and wait) until the health meters of whatever creature/s are put before us can go to zero before ours do. That's more of a chore than it is fun. I really wanted to like this game, but it's not meeting any of its creative potential at all, even though the artwork would suggest otherwise. There's just no creativity in the game design either! I want you devs to go hog wild, and then pull it back from there. Instead, I think you've started from a very safe place (copying other successful game mechanics) and iterated forward. That's not brave, or creative. At the very least, use your artists and put more story into the game to give the experience much needed context. Fascinate us with your world, and who we are in it. But ideally, do something more exciting with the gameplay. Move the camera at least. Try these ideas: - Recruit people you meet in the city for one-time adventures (non-upgradeable throw-away classes) for instance, a mechanic class to enable crafting on the fly to give better choices of cards, or a time-weaver class to undo bad draws or revive fallen soldiers. - Rescue missions. A creature has captured a team of 10 scavengers. Rescue them and they'll go exploring with you until you get back to the city. - Upgrade the city beyond just lanterns. Helping the residents and guiding their opinions through your deeds (siding with X faction, or helping Y community) makes them build city defences that help you in battle. Cannons. Fireballs. Fog. Shielded Zones. Be congratulated for using them by the citizens who built them when you return as a hero. The types of communities you help determine what gets made, and how reliable it is. A harmonious city equals well rounded defenses. Side with the workers and get strong defenses, but with little power. Side with the nobles and get intense but unstable power. - Properly explain the importance of the city's residents to the purpose of an "elevator city". If you make me believe that there's a reason why a city of people exists to run a giant elevator, then I'll get on board, but to do so you'd need to give us a run-up as to who even came up with the idea and how it came to be. (Same goes with the reason for the giant lady). - Gain intelligence from the bodies of the creatures. Collect carcasses and study them in labs to find out what's causing these creatures to grow into these things, or where they come from, etc, and how to better defeat them. Incorporate the results into the gameplay. Use these discoveries to advance the story. Create a class of warriors from the creatures, The Uncorrupted, and have parts of the city turn on you for using them because they feel they are untrustworthy. - Etc, etc... I know this is still in development, but you need to make some serious (and brave) decisions to allow this game to reach its full potential before you run out of funds. Sincerely, good luck.

Current game is pretty meh, combat is pretty boring with ridiculous damage spikes that will screw your run if you don't pull the correct card. Also the upgrade system is very uninteresting right now wow this card does 2 points more damage or give slightly more barrier. Maybe the devs should go play monster train 1/2 to see an upgrade/combat system that feels incredibly good. The game actively punishes you for having more then 1 unit on your side. Because they will pad out your deck with useless cards. Making you less likely to draw the upgraded cards/card need to mitigate a ton of damage. The only benefit to have other allied units is it "spreads" out the damage and extra auto attack. I find the game to be lacking in depth in all of its core features and it's hybrid foundation to be painfully flawed. Performance is terrible for what it is, UI is painful once you get draw rate up or enemies start hitting you with affliction cards. There are frustrating bugs, but honestly that's not going into my assessment. Many of the interactions are painfully unintuitive and punishing unless you memorize them or use a guide. Easy enough, but an outdated and silly selling point on games in 2026. Lets examine the game's own claims: Scavenge a dying world: Exploration is extremely limited, there are actually only 3 full rounds. Items impact is also limited as you progress. All that really matters is your RNG on deck & unit pulls. Everything else is moot. When you stack RNG on RNG on RNG with only 3 rounds, you actually severely limit the strategy available to you. The hybrid attempt of the game really falls flat given the limited depth and rounds. Recruit new squads of units by utilizing scavenged technology: This actually isn't really true, you really only recruit units once per round via acquiring a corrupted brain from a felled boss. The hybrid attempt of RNG technologies, Unit acquisition, deck building and city development in such a short (3 round game) really makes it feel like you get none of the features advertised to you. Outsmart your Foes: Honestly doesn't feel like you're doing this at all. Between the lackluster technology upgrades, and again, the hybrid attempt of deck building and RNG technologies, it doesn't feel like any of your choices really matter. Counter play is minimal without good cohesive pulls. Determine the Fate of the City: Again it's 3 rounds. You will not care about the city at all. Due to the layered RNG and limited rounds, all that matter is deck RNG. The current state of this game has you looking at your core pulls, and evaluating if you are restarting or not. Once you start sliding there is very little coming back, if at all. It's stomp or be stomped. Restart ASAP. If you find that a fun feature in game balance, well that's you. I know this is early access, but I find the core foundation of the game to be very flawed. You can't stack a hybrid approach with RNG on RNG on RNG and a 3 round game and expect it not to be a restart simulator.

Fun game! The long and short of it is that it has a good blend of deckbuilding with some light positional tactics to consider. Despite being in early access at the time of writing this, there is also a surprisingly nice variety of units to choose from and experiment with. Each faction also has different base mechanics, so even where there is overlap in unit archetypes between the two the playstyle is still varied. Like Slay the Spire and a number of other games, the focus becomes doing runs at higher and higher difficulties, which is done here via run modifiers. I appreciate that the modifiers often have a pro in addition to a con. This makes each run with different modifiers have a different shape and feel beyond just the ways in which they implement difficulty. I think that's a smart design decision! My main con is just that it is unfinished, which is to be expected in an early access. Definitely still playable, and definitely still fun! But the ending of a run can feel a little abrupt and there's definitely some places where the art isn't as polished. Overall I am really looking forward to what the final game will look like

Very cool little deck-builder strategy game! If you enjoy games like slay the spire, or my personal favorite, Vampire Crawlers, you will likely enjoy As We Descend. Like many of these deck builders, it comes with its own gameplay twist, in the form of combat zones - placing your units closer or further from the enemy affects which of your troops takes hits, and their ability to auto-attack the enemies between turns. This fun extra depth reminds me of games such as darkest dungeon, or the megaman battle network games. Positioning matters! I find it to be a charming and engaging interaction between gameplay elements, and recommend to all you strategy heads out there. I give it an early 8/10 on mechanical strength. I'll try to remember to update this review with my final thoughts once I've put some more time in, and as the game becomes more complete. (currently there is another faction in the works, and I'm not sure what else the devs may have planned)

Stumbled upon this game during the summer sale and it's been such a pleasant surprise! The best way I can describe it is a mix of Slay the Spire deckbuilding/upgrading and Darkest Dungeon positional combat, all wrapped up in a steampunk, City of Ember-esque package. The art style and themes are fantastic. As I said before, the gameplay takes a lot of inspiration from Slay the Spire, but this isn't a bad thing. If you've played either Spire game, the flow of combat will feel familiar and easily accessible, at least at its foundations. Layered on top of this are different mechanical systems that really add to the depth of the gameplay. I won't go into all of these, but by far my favorite is the weak point system. If you are able to stagger an enemy by breaking a stagger threshold, they are briefly stunned, and you can target a weak point to do extra damage. What's really cool is that some enemies have additional weak points that, instead of dealing extra damage, impact how the enemy behaves in some way. Maybe it disables a shield they were using, or decreases the effectiveness of heals targeting the enemy. There's a ton of content here, and with a third playable faction on the way, there's a lot to dig into. Really glad I came across this gem!

我运气非常好地购买了这款游戏。之前我还犹豫不决，但买下来之后的这九个小时，真是停不下来。 这款游戏的机制实际上设计得非常优秀。把卡片束缚到不同的角色上，实际上相比于旧的体系来说，可控性更强。但是很可惜，目前对这一点的发挥还不足够,游戏通过限制玩家可选项来提高游戏难度,但这导致了当前想要凑到自己喜欢的阵容非常困难。游戏流程不算很长,我觉得我很难在游戏结束前凑够我喜欢的卡组和阵容.这让游戏结束的非常遗憾,也许可以添加更多的层数,或者适当地提高随机奖励的可选性,这可以让游戏玩得起来更有趣,就像设计师应该已经想到了选择不同的远征或是是城镇互动来选择不同的奖励这一点,但做的又没有那么放开,总觉得缺点意思. 局外养成机制实际上非常有趣,但是开放和可自定义的程度实在是太浅了,不同的游戏难度都配备对应的加成和削弱，这点设计得非常棒，并且这是动态可选的。我真希望所有的开始状态都可以自定义。例如游戏难度等级可以由选择的真意和简易的总和来决定,这样就可以让我在开始的时候，来选择一些我希望能够尝试到的流派进行游玩。 这款游戏的底子非常不错，期待后续内容的加入,也希望后续这款游戏能够玩起来更爽快一些。

Last update made this incredibly luck based as there are no reliable ways to cull decks, get cards or otherwise make choices. The idea as stated was to give players more choices and have the choices matter more, but generally it's just reduced the amount of choices made from 20 to 8 and not made any of the choices meaningfully better. The other idea was that you can use items to multi stack on those 8 choices, but they reduced the amount of expeditions/expedition scavengers meaning you have less choices, those choices are random mostly, and you get less from dealing with more dangerous missions. Pre update, each run was basically doable with minor errors if you messed up or otherwise got unlucky. Higher difficulties made sense because it was for challenge sake and the base game wasn't easy but also wasn't hard. Now even at basic difficulty it's just nonsensically rng based and if you get even a bit behind because of poor rolls it snowballs hard with little chance to recover.
